title: Choose confidence, build the proof
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What proof are you waiting for before you feel confident?
A student said that a failed attempt would affect his confidence at first, or perhaps make him more confident because he learned and now has more to draw from.
I said that an optimistic person says: I choose confidence and I build proof. We tend to think proof and evidence are out of our control.
A student asked: are you saying the proof we base our confidence on is not up to us, or that it is?
I said that the answer is that it is up to you: you act, collect results and build the proof.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you want to feel confident about.
Write the proof you are waiting for.
Write three actions that would create it.
Write one thing you have already proved.
Write the date you will review the proof.

check.q: What did I say an optimistic person does?
What did a student say about a failure?
choices: It can affect confidence or teach

check.q: What did I say about proof?

recap: Choose confidence. Build the proof by acting.
